canonical_question: How might the 'irregular shape' of the V-powder affect the density and mechanical anisotropy of the final alloy compared to the spherical others?

question_variants.question: How might the 'irregular shape' of the V-powder affect the density and mechanical anisotropy of the final alloy compared to the spherical others?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text notes that the V-powder is irregularly shaped while others are spherical and flow well, but it does not provide specific data on how this irregular shape affects the density or mechanical anisotropy of the final alloy compared to the spherical ones.

answers.answer: All powder particles except the V-powder are predominantly spherical and show a good flowability.
answers.measurement_outcome: V-powder is irregular, others are spherical with good flowability
answers.mechanism: Spherical particles superior to irregular for flowability
answers.boundary_limitation: No quantitative data on density or anisotropy differences caused by shape
evidence_spans: W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is one of the first refractory metal high entropy alloys developed by Senkov et al. [ [18] ] and therefore also one of the best investigated ones.
For the experiments, a heterogeneous mixture of five single element powders was used to prepare the WMoTaNbV samples.
Spherical powder particles are in general superior to irregular shaped particles with respect to flowability and are consequently preferable.
